related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

guidance: A geometry aid, not a scattering prediction: the page sizes a one-dimensional Schroeder diffuser from the quadratic residue sequence and reports no scattering or diffusion coefficient. Mounting, surface material, divider thickness and edge treatment all change the result. The speed of sound is fixed at 343 m/s (dry air at 20 °C), widths are the clear openings without dividers, and a well over 400 mm deep, a panel over 2,400 mm wide or a clear well under 10 mm is called out because it is hard to build in one piece.
method: The well count N is prime and well n, from 0 to N - 1, takes the quadratic residue s_n = n² mod N, so the sequence repeats every N wells. Each well is d_n = lambda0/(2N) * s_n deep, where lambda0 = c/f0 is the wavelength at the design frequency, so the deepest well follows the largest residue, which for some primes is not (N - 1)/2. The clear well width is w = c/(2 * f_upper), half a wavelength at the highest frequency the panel has to scatter, because a wider well reflects specularly rather than scattering; the panel clear width is N * w. Lengths are millimetres, rounded to 0.01 mm. The design frequency is limited to 20 to 8,000 Hz and the upper frequency to 40 to 20,000 Hz, the upper frequency must be above the design frequency, and the well count is one of the twelve primes from 5 to 43. Dividers, frame, mounting and material are excluded, and the page reads no audio and makes no network request.

sources.title: CCRMA, Stanford - The Quadratic Residue Diffuser: s_n = n² mod N and the well depth d_n = lambda0/(2N) s_n
Atelier Crescendo - Quadratic Residue Diffusers (QRDs) explained: the depths set the low end and the clear well width is half a wavelength at the highest frequency
Wikipedia - Diffusion (acoustics): Schroeder's number-theoretic diffusers and their use beside absorption
